title: How it works
description: Every requirement of the assignment, the clarifications from the Mad Devs recruiter and the author’s decisions — with how each one is implemented and how to check it.

sections.title: 1. Task (assignment)
items: A meeting room booking interface within a working day. Working hours are 09:00–18:00.
The user can: pick a date; see existing bookings for that date; choose start and end time; create, edit and delete a booking.
Display format is up to the developer (list, timeline, slot grid or day calendar). Chosen: a day timeline with booking blocks, a 30-minute grid and a red line for the current time.

sections.title: 2. What the app does
items: Date selection: ← → arrows by day, a calendar, a “Today” button.
Bookings of the day on a 09:00–18:00 timeline.
Create: the “New booking” button (first free time) or a click on a free cell (its time).
Edit: click a booking — date, time and title can be changed; after saving the schedule switches to the booking date.
Delete: the “Delete” button in the booking form, with confirmation.
The selected date lives in the URL (/?date=2026-10-23): survives a reload and can be shared.
Drag on the timeline with the mouse to select a range; it never crosses another booking and is at most 2 hours. On phones — tap a cell.
Occupied time is disabled in the form: you cannot pick a start or end that would overlap another booking.
A day summary above the timeline: number of bookings, free time and the next free slot (click opens the form).
Keyboard shortcuts: ← → previous/next day, T today, N new booking (hints in button tooltips).
Theme: system, light or dark — a button in the header.
Neighbouring days are prefetched so the arrows are instant; while a day loads, the previous schedule stays dimmed instead of a skeleton.
Header with “Schedule” / “How it works” navigation and an RU / EN language switch.

sections.title: 3. Business rules and their implementation
items: 1. Start and end are within 09:00–18:00. Options outside the day are not offered; the server responds 422.
2. start < end. End options before the start are disabled; the server responds 422.
3. Minimum duration is 30 minutes. Shorter end options are disabled.
4. Maximum duration is 2 hours. Longer end options are disabled.
5. Bookings cannot overlap; touching borders is not a conflict: 10:00–11:00 and 11:00–12:00 are fine. An overlap is shown in the form before submitting; the server responds 409.

6. Past time cannot be booked. A past date is read-only (create button disabled, banner). Today the start is no earlier than the nearest future time on the 15-minute grid: at 14:20 the first available start is 14:30.
7. When editing, a booking does not conflict with itself.
8. The server may return 409 even if the UI considered the slot free. The UI shows a clear message in the form, refetches the bookings and keeps the form open — the entered data is preserved.
Additionally (recruiter clarification): bookings on weekdays only, Mon–Fri. Bookings that have started or ended cannot be changed or deleted — the block shows a lock.
Time is on a 15-minute step only — in the UI and on the server (10:07 → 422). A non-existent date (Nov 31) → 400.
All rules are one function shared by the form and the mock server: the form checks instantly, the server has the final word. The rules are covered by unit tests.

sections.title: 4. “What matters” (assignment)
items: Business logic and validation: one rules function + zod schemas for the form and the API; errors are shown under the specific field.
UI states: loading — a skeleton of the same shape; empty — a hint; error — a message and a “Retry” button; submitting — a spinner and disabled buttons.
Server errors: 400 (format), 404 (already deleted), 409 (conflict), 422 (rule violated), network down — clear messages in the interface language.
API and UI are separated: component → hook → entities/booking/api → axios. Server responses are validated with zod.
Readable TypeScript: strict mode, types inferred from zod; Feature-Sliced Design architecture with automated checks (ESLint, steiger, fsd-check).
Responsive and accessible: from 360px; labelled buttons and fields for screen readers, keyboard support, focus management in dialogs, clear error messages.

sections.title: 5. Stack and mock API (assignment)
items: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript.
Styling and UI: Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, lucide icons.
Data: TanStack Query + axios; forms: react-hook-form + zod; screen state: zustand; translations: next-intl.
Tests: vitest (unit) and Playwright (e2e).
Mock API — Next.js Route Handlers with in-memory storage. A real backend, auth and database are not required by the assignment.
The network layer is separated from the UI: switching to a real API is the NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL variable.

sections.title: 6. API (assignment contract)
items: GET /api/bookings?date=YYYY-MM-DD → 200 Booking[]
POST /api/bookings → 201 Booking | 400 | 409 | 422
PATCH /api/bookings/:id → 200 Booking | 400 | 404 | 409 | 422
DELETE /api/bookings/:id → 204 | 404 | 422
Booking = { id, date: YYYY-MM-DD, start: HH:mm, end: HH:mm, title? }
Error: { code, message, field? }. The message is in the language from the Accept-Language header.
The X-Time-Zone header carries the browser time zone: the server uses it to determine “now” for the past-time rule.
Dates are checked against the calendar (2026-11-31 → 400); format errors come in the interface language.

sections.title: 7. Clarifications from the Mad Devs recruiter

qa.q: Which time zone defines working hours and past time?
Bookings Mon–Fri only or any day?
It is 14:20 — can a booking start at 14:20 or at the nearest future time?
Can a booking that has started or ended be edited or deleted?
Is a 15-minute step enough or is arbitrary time needed?
When editing, can the date be changed or only time and title?
Should public holidays be taken into account?
In what format should the AI chat be submitted?
Random 409 in the mock, in-memory storage, a documentation page, auth, language, tests, booking horizon, extra features?

sections.title: 8. Author’s decisions
items: No authentication (assignment: “auth is not required”): any user can change or delete any booking.
Booking time is stored without a time zone (HH:mm) — all users are in one office. The browser time zone defines “now” and is sent to the server.
Public holidays are ignored; there is no booking horizon limit.
Conflict 409 is reproducible: the mock server returns 409 for about every fifth create (MOCK_CONFLICT_RATE=0.2) and puts a “Taken by a colleague” booking on that time.
Data is stored in server memory and resets on restart — enough for a demo.

Important for the Vercel demo: the server runs as several independent instances, each with its own memory. Two consecutive requests may hit different instances — a booking you just created may sometimes “disappear” after a refresh or reappear. This is a limitation of the mock storage, not of the app logic; with a real backend or shared storage (Redis/DB) it does not happen.
Language: Russian (main) and English, a switch in the header, the choice is remembered; the server responds in the interface language.
Booking title is optional, up to 80 characters.
Tests: unit — business rules; e2e — create, edit, delete, conflict 409, load error, past date, weekend, language.
This documentation page — requested by the author, agreed with the recruiter.

sections.title: 9. How to check manually
items: Create: click a free cell → the form opens with that time → “Book”.
Edit: click a booking → change date, time or title → “Save”.
Delete: click a booking → “Delete” → confirm.
Range select: press the mouse on free time and drag up or down — a frame shows the range, releasing opens the form.
URL date: switch to another day and reload — the day is kept.
Keys: ← → T N on the schedule page.
Note: the random 409 is a simulation, not a bug. If creating a booking shows “taken by another user”, that is intended — retry with another time.
Conflict 409: create bookings — about every fifth gets 409. The message appears in the form, a “Taken by a colleague” booking appears on the timeline, your input stays.
Overlap: pick a time taken by another booking — an error under the field before submitting.
Past time: ← to yesterday — read-only; today past cells are grey.
Weekends: go to Saturday with the arrows — a “Weekend” banner, creation disabled.
Load error: enable Offline in DevTools and change the date — “Retry” appears.
Language: the RU / EN switch in the header; the choice survives a reload.
